editorial:
Imagine waking up in a future where everything is run by giant, blinking computers that make funny bleeping and booping noises. In this world, women are the ones in charge of all the technology, and they have become cold and robotic in the process. Then along comes Yockoo, a wild boy from the bush who carries around a bag of dried fruits. He is the complete opposite of this sterile, digital world. It is a quirky, colorful setup that feels more like a strange dream than a typical sci-fi movie, and it keeps you guessing about how these two opposite worlds will clash.

You will love how the movie plays with the idea of nature versus technology. The acting is fun, and seeing the women slowly rediscover their feelings because of Yockoo is pretty funny. While it is a bit slow at times, the weird visuals make up for it. If you enjoy oddball comedies from the sixties, you should definitely check this out.
endingExplained: In the final scenes, the women completely drop their cold, computer-driven personas. They realize they miss their natural instincts and femininity. To celebrate Yockoo and his rugged charm, they go to a local museum to find old cooking tools. They use these ancient utensils to cook him a massive feast made entirely out of his dried fruits. It ends on a happy note where love and nature win over the cold machines.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves vintage oddities and satire about technology.
